## Workflow overview

**Question.** Which public water systems in Michigan are most at risk of PFAS contamination, and how do distance to known PFAS sites, aquifer type and soil permeability explain it?

**How the analysis flows**

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["1. Load data<br/>public water, PFAS sites, aquifers, gSSURGO soil"] --> B["2. Spatial joins<br/>aquifer, soil permeability, nearest PFAS site"]
  B --> C["3. Join audit<br/>what matched, what is missing, why"]
  C --> D["4. Location-level exploration<br/>hazard by aquifer, system type, distance, permeability"]
  D --> E["5. Aquifer and soil vs. risk (no distance)<br/>then pathway analysis with PFAS-site distance"]
  E --> F["6. Roll up to water systems<br/>max Hazard Index per system"]
  F --> G["7. Baseline<br/>log-linear model"]
  G --> H["8. Zero-inflated Tweedie"]
  H --> I["9. Hurdle<br/>detection + severity"]
  I --> J["10. Automatic selection<br/>AIC / BIC, LASSO cross-check"]
  J --> K["11. Model comparison<br/>+ spatial check"]
  K --> L["12. Conclusions and limits"]
```

**Key decisions in one place**

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Unit of analysis | Water system, using its worst location (`max_hazard`) | A public-health read should not let clean samples average away a hotspot |
| Outcome | `log(1 + max_hazard)` for linear models; raw `max_hazard` for Tweedie | 86% of readings are exactly zero and the rest are right-skewed |
| Distance | `log(1 + distance)` to the nearest known PFAS site, no cap; for the extended models taken from the system's highest-Hazard-Index location (`DISTANCE_BASIS`) | Uses the full range; the log compresses the long tail; same spot as the aquifer and soil |
| Soil | Permeability (harmonic mean of `ksat` over the top 100 cm, weighted by component percent, log10 scale) plus drainage class, hydrologic group, water table and bedrock depth, slope, organic carbon, available water storage and the droughty flag, all at the system's highest-Hazard-Index location | Layers act in series, and permeability spans orders of magnitude; the selection decides which other soil variables matter |
| Model order | Baseline, then zero-inflated Tweedie, then hurdle | Simple to flexible; each is compared on the same systems |
| Variable selection | Automatic backward elimination over all candidates, soil included; `n_hex_ids` always kept | AIC and BIC both run; the criterion used downstream is chosen automatically (BIC when there are fewer than 20 detected systems per candidate variable); `SELECTION_MODE` can force one |
| Rows | Systems with an aquifer match and a permeability value | AIC/BIC need every candidate model on the same rows |

**Packages used:** tidyverse, janitor, sf, tidymodels, glmmTMB (Tweedie), glmnet (LASSO), terra (soil map, first run only) and spdep (optional spatial check).

## Soil data (gSSURGO)
The soil data is the Michigan gSSURGO geodatabase (`gSSURGO_MI.gdb`) from USDA-NRCS, downloaded from the [NRCS gSSURGO Box folder](https://nrcs.app.box.com/v/soils/folder/233398887779?page=2). The geodatabase has only **one map layer** (`MUPOLYGON`, the soil map). Every soil property sits in separate tables that link to it by key, so the polygons themselves carry IDs and no soil values.

```{r}
# Layers and tables inside the gSSURGO geodatabase, with row counts and geometry types
st_layers("gSSURGO_MI.gdb")
```

The geodatabase has 78 layers, some have geometry type as NA meaning there is a plain table with no map shape that is no mupolygon also some have crs NA because the tables are non map

```{r}
# Soil map polygons (1.2M in total); only the first 1,000 are read here, just to see the column
# names and types. They are NOT a sample of the state: the map and the join below use ALL polygons
mupolygon_sample <- st_read("gSSURGO_MI.gdb",
                            query = "SELECT * FROM MUPOLYGON LIMIT 1000", quiet = TRUE)
glimpse(mupolygon_sample)
```

```{r}
# Only the layers used in this analysis
tibble(layer_name = st_layers("gSSURGO_MI.gdb")$name,
       features   = st_layers("gSSURGO_MI.gdb")$features) |>
  filter(layer_name %in% c("MUPOLYGON", "mapunit", "muaggatt", "Valu1", "component", "chorizon"))

```

### What each soil table is and how it is used

| Table | Rows | One row represents | Key fields | Used for | Importance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MUPOLYGON` | 1,207,754 | A soil map polygon (a shape on the map) | `MUKEY` | Matching each sampling location to a soil map unit, and drawing the soil map | Essential |
| `mapunit` | 10,664 | A soil map unit (a named group of soils) | `mukey` | Reference names only; no model variable comes from it | Low |
| `muaggatt` | 10,664 | A map unit, with ready-made summaries | `mukey` | Drainage class, hydrologic group, water table depth, bedrock depth, slope | High |
| `Valu1` | 10,664 | A map unit, with pre-computed values | `mukey` | Organic carbon, available water storage, droughty flag | Medium |
| `component` | 36,240 | A soil type inside a map unit | `mukey`, `cokey`, `comppct_r` | Linking map units to soil layers; `comppct_r` (percent of the map unit) is the weight when averaging | High |
| `chorizon` | 165,958 | A soil layer (horizon) of a soil type | `cokey`, `ksat_r`, `hzdept_r`, `hzdepb_r` | The only source of permeability (`ksat_r`) | High |

The tables connect in one chain: a sampling location falls inside a `MUPOLYGON` polygon, which gives its `MUKEY`. `muaggatt`, `Valu1` and `mapunit` have one row per `MUKEY`, so they join directly. Permeability takes extra steps: `chorizon` layers (linked by `cokey`) roll up to `component`, then to the map unit. About 1.2 million polygons point to only about 10,000 distinct map units, so many polygons share the same soil properties.

```{r}
# One row per soil map unit: map unit names and status
mapunit <- st_read("gSSURGO_MI.gdb", layer = "mapunit", quiet = TRUE) |> as_tibble()
glimpse(mapunit)
```

```{r}
# One row per map unit: aggregated soil properties (drainage, water table, bedrock depth, etc.)
muaggatt <- st_read("gSSURGO_MI.gdb", layer = "muaggatt", quiet = TRUE) |> as_tibble()
glimpse(muaggatt)
```

```{r}
# One row per map unit: pre-computed values (organic carbon, available water, crop indices)
valu1 <- st_read("gSSURGO_MI.gdb", layer = "Valu1", quiet = TRUE) |> as_tibble()
glimpse(valu1)
```

```{r}
# One row per soil component (several components can share a map unit)
component <- st_read("gSSURGO_MI.gdb", layer = "component", quiet = TRUE) |> as_tibble()
glimpse(component)
```

```{r}
# One row per soil horizon (layer) of a component; holds the permeability column ksat_r
chorizon <- st_read("gSSURGO_MI.gdb", layer = "chorizon", quiet = TRUE) |> as_tibble()
glimpse(chorizon)
```

The soil tables fit together like this: `MUPOLYGON` (the map, about 1.2 million polygons) points to about 10,664 distinct map units through `MUKEY`, so many polygons share the same soil properties. `mapunit`, `muaggatt` and `Valu1` have one row per soil map unit (linked to the polygons by `mukey`), `component` has one row per soil type inside a map unit, and `chorizon` has one row per soil layer inside a component (linked by `cokey`). Permeability lives in `chorizon`.

## Spatial Joins of aquifer, soil, public water and pfas sites

### Attaching aquifer characteristics to public_water1

```{r}
# Collapse to one row per unique sampling location and convert to spatial points
water_locations <- public_water1 |>
  distinct(hex_id, longitude, latitude) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

water_locations_proj <- st_transform(water_locations, st_crs(aquifer))
```

```{r}
# Attach aquifer attributes to each location by spatial join, then drop back to a plain table
water_aquifer <- water_locations_proj |>
  st_join(aquifer |> select(AQU_UNIT, AQU_CHAR)) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(hex_id, AQU_UNIT, AQU_CHAR)
```

```{r}
# n_locations = total sampling locations; n_missing_aquifer = locations with no aquifer match
water_aquifer |>
  summarise(
    n_locations       = n(),
    n_missing_aquifer = sum(is.na(AQU_UNIT)),
    pct_missing       = round(mean(is.na(AQU_UNIT)) * 100, 1)
  )
```

```{r}
# Pull out the locations that failed to match an aquifer polygon
unmatched <- water_locations_proj |>
  st_join(aquifer |> select(AQU_UNIT, AQU_CHAR)) |>
  filter(is.na(AQU_UNIT))

nrow(unmatched)   # should be 77

unmatched |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(hex_id, longitude, latitude)
```

```{r}
# Map of the unmatched points 
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = aquifer, fill = "grey90", color = "grey60") +
  geom_sf(data = unmatched, color = "#eb6834", size = 1.5) +
  labs(title = "Public-water locations with no aquifer match") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Attaching soil characteristics (gSSURGO) to public_water1

The gSSURGO geodatabase works in two steps: each sampling location is matched by point-in-polygon to a soil map unit (its `MUKEY`), and then `MUKEY` is used to join the soil attribute tables. Soil permeability is built first, on its own, so it can be inspected and mapped before any join happens.

#### Soil permeability (saturated hydraulic conductivity)

Permeability here is the saturated hydraulic conductivity `ksat_r` (micrometers per second): how fast water, and anything dissolved in it, can move down through the soil. It is stored per soil horizon, so it has to be averaged up to the map unit.

```{r}
# Per component: harmonic-mean ksat over the top 100 cm layers in series, so the tightest layer limits flow
component_ksat <- chorizon |>
  mutate(thick_cm = pmax(0, pmin(hzdepb_r, 100) - pmax(hzdept_r, 0))) |>
  filter(thick_cm > 0, !is.na(ksat_r), ksat_r > 0) |>
  group_by(cokey) |>
  summarise(ksat_100cm = sum(thick_cm) / sum(thick_cm / ksat_r), .groups = "drop")

# Per map unit: components weighted by their percent of the map unit, then the standard NRCS classes
soil_perm <- component |>
  inner_join(component_ksat, by = "cokey") |>
  group_by(mukey) |>
  summarise(ksat_100cm = weighted.mean(ksat_100cm, comppct_r, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    perm_class = cut(
      ksat_100cm,
      breaks = c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, Inf), right = FALSE,
      labels = c("Very low", "Low", "Moderately low", "Moderately high", "High", "Very high")
    ),
    perm_code = as.integer(perm_class)
  )

glimpse(soil_perm)
```

```{r}
# n_mukeys_with_ksat = map units that ended up with a permeability value; then the spread of values
soil_perm |>
  summarise(
    n_mukeys_with_ksat = n(),
    min_ksat    = round(min(ksat_100cm), 3),
    median_ksat = round(median(ksat_100cm), 2),
    mean_ksat   = round(mean(ksat_100cm), 2),
    max_ksat    = round(max(ksat_100cm), 1)
  )
```

```{r}
# Coverage: n_mukeys_total = all map units in muaggatt; n_mukeys_no_ksat = those with no permeability value
muaggatt |>
  summarise(
    n_mukeys_total   = n_distinct(mukey),
    n_mukeys_no_ksat = sum(!mukey %in% soil_perm$mukey),
    pct_no_ksat      = round(100 * mean(!mukey %in% soil_perm$mukey), 1)
  )
```

```{r}
# n_mukeys = map units in each permeability class
soil_perm |>
  count(perm_class, name = "n_mukeys") |>
  mutate(share = round(n_mukeys / sum(n_mukeys), 3))
```

```{r}
# Distribution of map-unit permeability; log scale because values span several orders of magnitude
soil_perm |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ksat_100cm)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#2a78d6") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Soil Permeability of Michigan Map Units (top 100 cm)",
    x = "ksat, top 100 cm (micrometers per second, log scale)", y = "Number of map units"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The classes follow the NRCS scale in micrometers per second: very low is under 0.01, low 0.01 to 0.1, moderately low 0.1 to 1, moderately high 1 to 10, high 10 to 100, and very high is 100 or more. The depth average uses a harmonic mean because water moves down through layers in series, so the tightest layer controls the flow, while components side by side are averaged by their percent. Map units with no usable `ksat_r` (for example open water or some urban land) have no row in `soil_perm` and will come out as missing after the join. Each value is an average over a map unit, so it describes the typical soil of that unit, not a single spot, and it covers only the top 100 cm, while wells often draw from deeper deposits.

#### Map of soil permeability

```{r}
# The 1.2M-polygon read and rasterize is slow, so the 1 km grid is cached to an RDS file
if (file.exists("soil_perm_raster.rds")) {
  perm_raster_df <- readRDS("soil_perm_raster.rds")
} else {
  soil_vect <- terra::vect("gSSURGO_MI.gdb", layer = "MUPOLYGON",
                           query = "SELECT MUKEY FROM MUPOLYGON")
  soil_vect$perm_code <- soil_perm$perm_code[match(soil_vect$MUKEY, soil_perm$mukey)]

  perm_grid   <- terra::rast(terra::ext(soil_vect), resolution = 1000, crs = terra::crs(soil_vect))
  perm_raster <- terra::rasterize(soil_vect, perm_grid, field = "perm_code")

  perm_raster_df <- as.data.frame(perm_raster, xy = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    set_names(c("x", "y", "perm_code"))

  saveRDS(perm_raster_df, "soil_perm_raster.rds")
}
```

```{r}
# Statewide soil permeability class on a 1 km grid
perm_raster_df |>
  mutate(perm_class = factor(perm_code, levels = 1:6, labels = levels(soil_perm$perm_class))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, fill = perm_class)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Permeability", direction = -1) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Soil Permeability in the Top 100 cm (gSSURGO)") +
  theme_void()
```

#### Joining soil to the sampling locations

```{r}
# Point-in-polygon against 1.2M soil polygons is slow, so it runs once and is cached to a CSV
if (file.exists("water_mukey.csv")) {
  water_mukey <- read_csv("water_mukey.csv", col_types = cols(MUKEY = col_character()))
} else {
  mupolygon <- st_read("gSSURGO_MI.gdb", query = "SELECT MUKEY FROM MUPOLYGON", quiet = TRUE)

  water_mukey <- st_transform(water_locations, st_crs(mupolygon)) |>
    st_join(mupolygon) |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    distinct(hex_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   # a point on a polygon boundary can match twice
    select(hex_id, MUKEY)

  write_csv(water_mukey, "water_mukey.csv")
}
```

```{r}
# n_missing_soil = locations outside every soil polygon (e.g. open water, shoreline)
water_mukey |>
  summarise(
    n_locations    = n(),
    n_missing_soil = sum(is.na(MUKEY)),
    pct_missing    = round(mean(is.na(MUKEY)) * 100, 1)
  )
```

```{r}
# Soil attribute tables hold one row per MUKEY, so these joins cannot duplicate locations
water_soil <- water_mukey |>
  left_join(
    muaggatt |> select(mukey, drclassdcd, hydgrpdcd, wtdepannmin, brockdepmin, slopegradwta),
    by = c("MUKEY" = "mukey")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    valu1 |> select(mukey, soc0_150, aws0_150, droughty),
    by = c("MUKEY" = "mukey")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    soil_perm |> select(mukey, ksat_100cm, perm_class),
    by = c("MUKEY" = "mukey")
  )

glimpse(water_soil)
```

```{r}
# pct_missing per soil attribute (urban and water map units often carry no soil data)
water_soil |>
  summarise(across(
    c(drclassdcd, hydgrpdcd, wtdepannmin, brockdepmin, slopegradwta,
      soc0_150, aws0_150, droughty, ksat_100cm),
    ~ round(mean(is.na(.x)) * 100, 1)
  ))
```

#### Auditing the soil join

**Procedure**

1. Follow the locations through the join stage by stage: inside a soil polygon, then a map unit record, then a permeability value.
2. Separate the two reasons a location can end up without permeability.
3. Check how many locations share a map unit.

**Key points**

- A location is lost either because it sits outside every soil polygon (open water, shoreline) or because its map unit has no usable `ksat_r` (urban land, pits).
- Locations that share a map unit get an identical soil value, so soil is a coarser measure than the number of locations suggests.

```{r}
# Join funnel: each stage keeps only the locations that made it through the previous one
water_soil |>
  summarise(
    n_all_locations      = n(),
    n_in_soil_polygon    = sum(!is.na(MUKEY)),
    n_with_map_unit_data = sum(!is.na(drclassdcd) | !is.na(hydgrpdcd) | !is.na(slopegradwta)),
    n_with_permeability  = sum(!is.na(ksat_100cm))
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "stage", values_to = "n_locations") |>
  mutate(pct_of_all = round(100 * n_locations / first(n_locations), 1))
```

```{r}
# Why a location has no permeability: outside every soil polygon, or inside one with no usable ksat
water_soil |>
  mutate(permeability_status = case_when(
    is.na(MUKEY)      ~ "Outside soil polygons",
    is.na(ksat_100cm) ~ "In a soil polygon, no permeability value",
    TRUE              ~ "Has permeability"
  )) |>
  count(permeability_status, name = "n_locations") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n_locations / sum(n_locations), 1))
```

```{r}
# Map units behind the "no permeability value" locations (urban land, water and pits are typical)
water_soil |>
  filter(!is.na(MUKEY), is.na(ksat_100cm)) |>
  left_join(mapunit |> select(mukey, muname), by = c("MUKEY" = "mukey")) |>
  count(muname, name = "n_locations", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
```

```{r}
# How many distinct map units the locations fall in, and how many locations share one
water_soil |>
  filter(!is.na(MUKEY)) |>
  count(MUKEY, name = "n_locations_in_map_unit") |>
  summarise(
    n_distinct_map_units    = n(),
    median_locations_per_mu = median(n_locations_in_map_unit),
    max_locations_per_mu    = max(n_locations_in_map_unit),
    n_map_units_shared      = sum(n_locations_in_map_unit > 1)
  )
```

```{r}
# Sampling locations colored by the permeability class of the soil they sit on
water_locations |>
  left_join(water_soil |> select(hex_id, perm_class), by = "hex_id") |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = aquifer, fill = "grey95", color = "grey75") +
  geom_sf(aes(color = perm_class), size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Permeability", direction = -1, na.value = "#eb6834") +
  labs(title = "Public-water sampling locations by soil permeability") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#### Do the sampling locations represent the whole state's soils?

```{r}
# Share of the whole state (by area) in each permeability class, from the full 1 km grid
state_share <- perm_raster_df |>
  filter(!is.na(perm_code)) |>
  count(perm_code, name = "n_cells") |>
  mutate(
    perm_class = factor(perm_code, levels = 1:6, labels = levels(soil_perm$perm_class)),
    share      = n_cells / sum(n_cells),
    source     = "Whole state (by area)"
  )

# Share of sampling locations sitting on each permeability class
site_share <- water_soil |>
  filter(!is.na(perm_class)) |>
  count(perm_class, name = "n_locations") |>
  mutate(
    share  = n_locations / sum(n_locations),
    source = "Water sampling locations"
  )

# Side-by-side comparison of the two shares
bind_rows(
  select(state_share, perm_class, share, source),
  select(site_share,  perm_class, share, source)
) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = perm_class, y = share, fill = source)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Whole state (by area)" = "#2a78d6",
                               "Water sampling locations" = "#eb6834")) +
  labs(
    title = "Soil permeability: whole state vs. sampling locations",
    x = "Permeability class", y = "Share", fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

This compares the whole state, using every soil polygon through the 1 km grid, with where the water systems are sampled. Similar bars mean the sampling locations cover Michigan's soils evenly. Differences are expected to some degree, because water systems cluster in towns while large forested areas have few, so a gap does not by itself mean a bias.

The soil columns kept for now are permeability (`ksat_100cm` and its class), drainage class (`drclassdcd`), hydrologic group (`hydgrpdcd`), minimum annual water table depth (`wtdepannmin`), depth to bedrock (`brockdepmin`), slope (`slopegradwta`), organic carbon to 150 cm (`soc0_150`), available water storage to 150 cm (`aws0_150`) and a droughty flag (`droughty`). A missing `wtdepannmin` commonly means no water table was recorded in the soil profile, so it is not always plain missing data.

### Connect public water to nearby PFAS sites (distance-based metric)

```{r}
# Convert PFAS sites to spatial points, reproject to meters to match the aquifer CRS
pfas_sites_sf   <- pfas_sites1 |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)
pfas_sites_proj <- st_transform(pfas_sites_sf, st_crs(aquifer))
```

```{r}
# For every water location, find the single closest PFAS site and its distance in meters
nearest_idx  <- st_nearest_feature(water_locations_proj, pfas_sites_proj)
nearest_dist <- st_distance(water_locations_proj, pfas_sites_proj[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)

water_pfas_nearest <- water_locations_proj |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(hex_id) |>
  mutate(
    distance_to_nearest_site_m = as.numeric(nearest_dist),
    nearest_site_facility = pfas_sites_proj$facility[nearest_idx],
    nearest_site_type     = pfas_sites_proj$type[nearest_idx]
  )
```

```{r}
# Count how many PFAS sites (not just the nearest one) fall within a 5km radius
within_5km <- st_is_within_distance(water_locations_proj, pfas_sites_proj, dist = 5000)

water_pfas_nearest <- water_pfas_nearest |>
  mutate(
    n_sites_within_5km = lengths(within_5km),
    pfas_site_nearby    = n_sites_within_5km > 0
  )
```

```{r}
# Classify the PFAS sites themselves by aquifer, for a sites-level (not water-level) view
pfas_sites_aquifer <- pfas_sites_proj |>
  st_join(aquifer |> select(AQU_UNIT, AQU_CHAR)) |>
  st_drop_geometry()
```

### Combine into one joined dataset

```{r}
# Attach the aquifer, soil and PFAS-proximity lookup tables onto every public_water1 row
modeling_data <- public_water1 |>
  left_join(water_aquifer, by = "hex_id") |>
  left_join(water_soil, by = "hex_id") |>
  left_join(water_pfas_nearest, by = "hex_id")

glimpse(modeling_data)
```


```{r}
# Inspect the raw aquifer codes and their full text descriptions before recoding
```

```{r}
# Map each AQU_UNIT code to a short, chart-friendly ordered label
modeling_data <- modeling_data |>
  mutate(
    aquifer_label = case_when(
      AQU_UNIT == "1"               ~ "I: Thin drift over bedrock",
      AQU_UNIT == "2"               ~ "II: Drift generally not an aquifer",
      AQU_UNIT %in% c("3a", "3aX")  ~ "IIIA: Interbedded, unconfined near surface",
      AQU_UNIT %in% c("3b", "3bX")  ~ "IIIB: Interbedded, variable near surface",
      AQU_UNIT == "4"               ~ "IV: Possible aquifer, undelineated",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    aquifer_label = factor(
      aquifer_label,
      levels = c(
        "I: Thin drift over bedrock",
        "II: Drift generally not an aquifer",
        "IIIA: Interbedded, unconfined near surface",
        "IIIB: Interbedded, variable near surface",
        "IV: Possible aquifer, undelineated"
      )
    )
  )

# n_locations = distinct hex_id sampling locations in each aquifer label
modeling_data |>
  distinct(hex_id, aquifer_label) |>
  count(aquifer_label, name = "n_locations", sort = TRUE)
```

## Exploratory Analysis of the Joined Dataset

Everything in this section works at the **hex_id which is the sampling location** for location-level modeling, before the system level analysis of the exact public water drinking sites are analysed

```{r}
# Collapse modeling_data down to one row per sampling location (drop the analyte-level rows)
location_level <- modeling_data |>
  distinct(hex_id, system_name, system_type, system_short, Hazard_Index,
           AQU_UNIT, aquifer_label,
           MUKEY, drclassdcd, hydgrpdcd, wtdepannmin, brockdepmin, slopegradwta,
           soc0_150, aws0_150, droughty, ksat_100cm, perm_class,
           distance_to_nearest_site_m, nearest_site_type, n_sites_within_5km, pfas_site_nearby)

# QA: n_rows_per_hex should be 1 for every hex_id (confirms one row per location)
location_level |>
  count(hex_id, name = "n_rows_per_hex") |>
  filter(n_rows_per_hex > 1)

nrow(location_level)
```

This chunk collapses modeling_data from 45,080 analyte-level rows down to 1,610 rows — one per sampling location by keeping only the columns that don't vary by analyte (Hazard_Index, aquifer, soil, distance, etc.) and dropping the duplicate rows that resulted from testing 28 different chemicals at each location.No hex_id ended up with more than one row and the final count is 1,610 rows.

### Soil permeability and the joined dataset (location grain)

**Procedure**

1. Check whether missing permeability clusters in particular system types or aquifers, and whether those locations look different on hazard.
2. Compare the Hazard Index across permeability classes, the same way it was compared across aquifer types.
3. Check how permeability overlaps with aquifer type and distance before it goes into the models.

**Key points**

- Models drop systems with no permeability, so it matters whether those systems are a random slice or a distinct group.
- Aquifer type and permeability describe related things (the geology and the soil above it), so some overlap is expected.
- This is exploration only; the models later decide whether permeability adds anything beyond distance and aquifer.

```{r}
# pct_missing_ksat by system type: if missing soil clusters in one type, dropping those systems biases the models
location_level |>
  group_by(system_short) |>
  summarise(
    n_locations      = n(),
    n_missing_ksat   = sum(is.na(ksat_100cm)),
    pct_missing_ksat = round(100 * mean(is.na(ksat_100cm)), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(pct_missing_ksat))
```

```{r}
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(aquifer_label)
```

```{r}
  summarise(
    n_locations  = n(),

    mean_hazard  = round(mean(Hazard_Index, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# Rank correlations: how much permeability overlaps with distance, and how it relates to Hazard Index directly
location_level |>
  filter(!is.na(ksat_100cm), !is.na(distance_to_nearest_site_m)) |>
  summarise(
    n_locations          = n(),
    spearman_ksat_dist   = round(cor(log10(ksat_100cm), log1p(distance_to_nearest_site_m), method = "spearman"), 3),
    spearman_ksat_hazard = round(cor(log10(ksat_100cm), Hazard_Index, method = "spearman"), 3)
  )
```

Read the tables together: a flat detection rate across permeability classes means permeability alone does not separate contaminated from clean locations, while a rising rate toward the permeable classes would match the idea that PFAS moves down faster through coarse soil. A correlation with distance close to zero means permeability brings information that distance does not already carry.

### Aquifer type and soil type vs. risk (no distance) (location grain)

Distance only makes sense for the **known PFAS sites**, because it measures how far a location is from a source. Aquifer and soil are different: they describe the **ground** the water comes from, so here each aquifer type and each soil type is compared with risk directly, with no distance in the picture.

**Procedure**

1. Keep locations with an aquifer type and, for the soil questions, a soil value.
2. For each aquifer type, permeability class, drainage class and hydrologic group, count locations and systems and measure the detection rate and the Hazard Index.
3. Express each group's detection rate relative to the overall rate (a risk ratio: 1 is average, above 1 is riskier than average).
4. Test whether the groups really differ, then cross aquifer type with permeability.
5. Fit ground-only logistic models (no distance) to see how much aquifer and soil explain on their own.

**Key points**

- A risk ratio compares a group with the average location, so it shows which ground types stand out, not just which have the most samples.
- Small groups give unstable rates, so read `n_locations` next to every percentage.
- Aquifer and soil belong to the **exact sampling location** (`hex_id`): each is the type of the polygon that location sits in, so the location is the natural unit for comparing ground types.
- A water system can have several `hex_id`s (1 to 9), and those can sit on different ground types, so a system can appear in more than one group. Counts of systems therefore do not add up across groups, and `n_water_systems` below counts a system once per group it appears in.
- Locations in the same system are not independent, so a model with a system effect is shown next to the plain one, and a system-level view uses only systems that sit on a single type.

```{r}
# Locations with a known aquifer; detected = any PFAS above zero. No distance variable is used in this section
ground_data <- location_level |>
  filter(!is.na(aquifer_label)) |>
  mutate(
    detected      = Hazard_Index > 0,
    aquifer_short = str_extract(as.character(aquifer_label), "^[^:]+"),
    log_ksat      = log10(ksat_100cm)
  )

# Helper: risk summary for any grouping variable; risk_ratio = group detection rate / overall rate
risk_by <- function(data, group_var) {
  data    <- data |> filter(!is.na({{ group_var }}))
  overall <- mean(data$detected, na.rm = TRUE)
  data |>
    group_by({{ group_var }}) |>
    summarise(
      n_locations     = n(),
      n_water_systems = n_distinct(system_name),
      n_detected      = sum(detected, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_systems_detected = n_distinct(system_name[detected %in% TRUE]),
      pct_detected    = round(100 * mean(detected, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      risk_ratio      = round(mean(detected, na.rm = TRUE) / overall, 2),
      mean_hazard     = round(mean(Hazard_Index, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      p90_hazard      = round(quantile(Hazard_Index, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Helper: bar chart of detection rate by group with n labels and a dashed line at the overall rate
plot_risk <- function(tbl, group_var, title, xlab) {
  ggplot(tbl, aes(x = {{ group_var }}, y = pct_detected)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#2a78d6", width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0("n=", n_locations)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 100 * sum(tbl$n_detected) / sum(tbl$n_locations), linetype = "dashed") +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = rev) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab, y = "% Locations Detected (dashed line = overall)") +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Helper: do the groups differ? chi-square (simulated p) on detection, Kruskal-Wallis on Hazard Index
group_test <- function(data, group_var, label) {
  d <- data |> filter(!is.na({{ group_var }}), !is.na(detected))
  g <- d |> pull({{ group_var }}) |> as.character()
  set.seed(123)
  tibble(
    factor              = label,
    n_groups            = n_distinct(g),
    n_locations         = nrow(d),
    p_detection_differs = signif(chisq.test(table(g, d$detected), simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 5000)$p.value, 3),
    p_hazard_differs    = signif(kruskal.test(d$Hazard_Index ~ factor(g))$p.value, 3)
  )
}
```

#### Matching ground type to the exact location

```{r}
# How many ground types does one system touch? One row per system, counted over its own hex_ids
system_ground_span <- ground_data |>
  group_by(system_name) |>
  summarise(
    n_hex_ids       = n(),
    n_aquifer_types = n_distinct(aquifer_short),
    n_perm_classes  = n_distinct(perm_class, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Of the systems with more than one location, how many straddle two or more aquifer types or permeability classes?
system_ground_span |>
  summarise(
    n_systems                    = n(),
    n_multi_location_systems     = sum(n_hex_ids > 1),
    n_span_2plus_aquifers        = sum(n_aquifer_types > 1),
    n_span_2plus_perm_classes    = sum(n_perm_classes > 1),
    pct_of_multi_span_aquifers   = round(100 * sum(n_aquifer_types > 1) / sum(n_hex_ids > 1), 1),
    pct_of_multi_span_perm       = round(100 * sum(n_perm_classes > 1) / sum(n_hex_ids > 1), 1)
  )
```

Because ground type is a property of the exact location, a system with several `hex_id`s is not one ground type by default. The counts above show how many systems straddle types. Where that number is small, assigning one type per system (the highest-Hazard-Index location, as the system-level models do) loses little; where it is large, the location-level tables below are the more faithful view, and the system-level view further down keeps only systems that sit on a single type.

```{r}
# System grain, clean assignment: keep only systems whose locations all sit on ONE type, then use the system's worst reading
system_risk_by <- function(data, group_var) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na({{ group_var }})) |>
    group_by(system_name) |>
    filter(n_distinct({{ group_var }}) == 1) |>
    summarise({{ group_var }} := first({{ group_var }}), n_hex_ids = n(),
              max_hazard = max(Hazard_Index, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by({{ group_var }}) |>
    summarise(
      n_water_systems           = n(),
      n_systems_detected        = sum(max_hazard > 0),
      pct_systems_detected      = round(100 * mean(max_hazard > 0), 1),
      mean_locations_per_system = round(mean(n_hex_ids), 2),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

system_risk_by(ground_data, aquifer_label) |> arrange(aquifer_label)
system_risk_by(ground_data, perm_class)    |> arrange(perm_class)
```

Compare these system rates with the location rates in the next tables. If they tell the same story, the finding does not depend on the difference between 1,610 `hex_id`s and about 1,500 systems.

#### Aquifer type and soil permeability together

```{r}
# Detection rate for each aquifer x permeability class (no distance); blank when fewer than 10 locations
ground_data |>
  filter(!is.na(perm_class)) |>
  group_by(aquifer_short, perm_class) |>
  summarise(n_locations = n(), pct_detected = round(100 * mean(detected, na.rm = TRUE), 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct_shown = if_else(n_locations >= 10, pct_detected, NA_real_)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = perm_class, y = aquifer_short, fill = pct_shown)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(n_locations >= 10, paste0(pct_detected, "%\nn=", n_locations), "")), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "% detected", direction = -1, na.value = "grey92") +
  labs(title = "Detection Rate by Aquifer Type and Soil Permeability",
       x = "Permeability class", y = "Aquifer type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
# Ground-only logistic models (no distance): how much do aquifer and permeability explain, alone and together?
ground_logit_data <- ground_data |>
  filter(!is.na(ksat_100cm)) |>
  mutate(detected_yes = as.integer(detected))

g_aquifer <- glm(detected_yes ~ aquifer_short,             data = ground_logit_data, family = binomial)
g_soil    <- glm(detected_yes ~ log_ksat,                  data = ground_logit_data, family = binomial)
g_both    <- glm(detected_yes ~ aquifer_short + log_ksat,  data = ground_logit_data, family = binomial)

# mcfadden_r2 = share of the null model's deviance explained (0.2 to 0.4 is a strong fit; near 0 means little)
tibble(
  model         = c("Aquifer only", "Permeability only", "Aquifer + permeability"),
  n_locations   = nrow(ground_logit_data),
  aic           = c(AIC(g_aquifer), AIC(g_soil), AIC(g_both)),
  bic           = c(BIC(g_aquifer), BIC(g_soil), BIC(g_both)),
  mcfadden_r2   = round(1 - c(g_aquifer$deviance, g_soil$deviance, g_both$deviance) / g_both$null.deviance, 3)
) |>
  mutate(across(c(aic, bic), \(x) round(x, 1)))
```

```{r}
# Does each ground factor add to the other? Small p-value = yes
anova(g_soil,    g_both, test = "Chisq")   # adding aquifer to permeability
anova(g_aquifer, g_both, test = "Chisq")   # adding permeability to aquifer

# Odds of detection; aquifer types are compared with the first type (I); log_ksat is per 10-fold more permeable soil
tidy(g_both, exponentiate = TRUE) |> arrange(p.value)
```

```{r}
# Same model with a random intercept per system, so locations of one system are not treated as independent
g_both_system <- glmmTMB(detected_yes ~ aquifer_short + log_ksat + (1 | system_name),
                         data = ground_logit_data, family = binomial)

# Odds ratios with and without the system effect; similar values mean the pattern is not an artefact of multi-location systems
left_join(
  tidy(g_both, exponentiate = TRUE) |> select(term, odds_ratio_plain = estimate, p_plain = p.value),
  summary(g_both_system)$coefficients$cond |>
    as_tibble(rownames = "term") |> janitor::clean_names() |>
    transmute(term, odds_ratio_system_effect = exp(estimate), p_system_effect = pr_z),
  by = "term"
) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

If the odds ratios barely move once each system gets its own intercept, the location-level result is not driven by systems that simply have more `hex_id`s. If they shrink or lose significance, treat the location tables as optimistic and lean on the system-level models.

Read the tables together. A risk ratio well above 1 with a decent `n_locations` marks a ground type that carries more detection than average, and a small p-value in the test table says the differences between groups are more than chance. The ground-only models then show how much aquifer and soil explain without any help from distance; a McFadden R-squared near zero would mean the ground type alone says little about where PFAS turns up, and any pattern is more likely driven by where the sources are.

### Connecting PFAS sites, soil permeability, aquifers and public water (location grain)

Distance applies only to the **known PFAS sites** (the source). Aquifer and soil were compared with risk on their own, with no distance, in the section above; this section adds the source link and checks whether the ground changes it. The analysis follows the path PFAS would take to a drinking-water location: it starts at a **known PFAS site** (the source), moves down through the **soil** (infiltration), is carried by the **aquifer** (transport), and is measured at the **public water location** (the receptor). Each step below adds one layer to the previous one.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  S["Known PFAS sites (source)<br/>distance to nearest site<br/>sites within 5 km"] --> SO["Soil permeability (infiltration)<br/>ksat, top 100 cm"]
  SO --> AQ["Aquifer type (transport)<br/>glacial drift class"]
  AQ --> W["Public water location (receptor)<br/>Hazard Index per hex_id"]
  W --> SY["Water system<br/>max Hazard Index"]
  SY --> M["Models<br/>baseline, Tweedie, hurdle"]
```

**Procedure**

1. Build one table of locations that have a distance, an aquifer and a permeability value, with distance bands and grouped permeability classes.
2. Step 1, source to receptor: detection rate by distance band.
3. Step 2, add the aquifer: detection rate by distance band within each aquifer type.
4. Step 3, add the soil: detection rate by distance band within each permeability group.
5. Step 4, all three together: aquifer and permeability combinations, split into near and far locations.
6. Map the pieces together and test whether permeability changes how much distance matters.

**Key points**

- Aquifer and soil permeability are measured **at the water location**, not at the PFAS site, so they describe the ground the water is drawn from, not the ground the contamination started in.
- Cells with fewer than 10 locations are left blank in the heatmaps, because their rates are not stable.
- This is a location-level exploration; locations in the same system share a system, so patterns here are a guide to what the system-level models should test.

```{r}
# One row per location with all three layers present; bands and groups make the cells large enough to read
pathway_data <- location_level |>
  filter(!is.na(aquifer_label), !is.na(perm_class), !is.na(distance_to_nearest_site_m)) |>
  mutate(
    detected       = Hazard_Index > 0,
    distance_band  = cut(distance_to_nearest_site_m, breaks = c(0, 5000, 15000, 30000, Inf),
                         labels = c("0-5 km", "5-15 km", "15-30 km", "30+ km"), include.lowest = TRUE),
    distance_group = factor(if_else(distance_to_nearest_site_m <= 15000, "Within 15 km", "Beyond 15 km"),
                            levels = c("Within 15 km", "Beyond 15 km")),
    aquifer_short  = str_extract(as.character(aquifer_label), "^[^:]+"),
    perm_group     = fct_collapse(
      perm_class,
      "Low (very low to moderately low)" = c("Very low", "Low", "Moderately low"),
      "Moderately high"                  = "Moderately high",
      "High / very high"                 = c("High", "Very high")
    )
  )

# Helper: share of locations with any detectable PFAS within any grouping
detect_by <- function(data, ...) {
  data |>
    group_by(...) |>
    summarise(n_locations = n(), pct_detected = round(100 * mean(detected), 1), .groups = "drop")
}

# n_locations per distance band (edit the breaks above if a band is too small)
pathway_data |> count(distance_band, name = "n_locations")
```

#### Step 1: PFAS site distance and detection

```{r}
# Detection rate and mean Hazard Index by distance band
by_distance <- pathway_data |>
  group_by(distance_band) |>
  summarise(
    n_locations  = n(),
    pct_detected = round(100 * mean(detected), 1),
    mean_hazard  = round(mean(Hazard_Index), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

by_distance
```

```{r}
ggplot(by_distance, aes(x = distance_band, y = pct_detected)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#eb6834", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("n=", n_locations)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Detection Rate by Distance to the Nearest Known PFAS Site",
       x = "Distance to nearest site", y = "% Locations Detected") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#### Step 2: add the aquifer

```{r}
# Detection rate for each distance band x aquifer type; blank when fewer than 10 locations
detect_by(pathway_data, aquifer_short, distance_band) |>
  mutate(pct_shown = if_else(n_locations >= 10, pct_detected, NA_real_)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = distance_band, y = aquifer_short, fill = pct_shown)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(n_locations >= 10, paste0(pct_detected, "%\nn=", n_locations), "")), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "% detected", direction = -1, na.value = "grey92") +
  labs(title = "Detection Rate by Distance and Aquifer Type",
       x = "Distance to nearest site", y = "Aquifer type") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#### Step 3: add the soil permeability

```{r}
# Detection rate across distance bands, one line per permeability group
detect_by(pathway_data, perm_group, distance_band) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = distance_band, y = pct_detected, color = perm_group, group = perm_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
```
